title: Module overview
body: This module opens the GR atlas by explaining why gravity is reinterpreted as spacetime geometry. It links the equivalence principle, local inertial frames, freely falling observers, and tidal gravity into the first conceptual bridge from special relativity to curvature.

title: Module overview
body: This module introduces the metric as a tensor field and the basic tensor-calculus tools needed to use it. The emphasis is on \(g_{\mu\nu}\), its inverse, and the invariant volume element as the first working language for curved spacetime.

title: Module overview
body: This module shows how the metric determines intervals, clock readings, lightlike directions, causal structure, and local flatness. It is the metric-geometry foundation for later geodesics, curvature, horizons, and field equations.

title: Module overview
body: This module introduces the geometric rule for comparing vectors at neighbouring events. Connections, Christoffel symbols, covariant derivatives, metric compatibility, vanishing torsion, and parallel transport provide the differentiation language needed for geodesics and curvature.

title: Module overview
body: This module connects spacetime geometry to physical free fall. Geodesics, their coordinate and variational equations, four-velocity, four-acceleration, and geodesic deviation distinguish inertial falling motion from supported motion and expose tidal curvature.

title: Module overview
body: This module defines spacetime curvature and its principal contractions. The Riemann, Ricci, scalar, and Einstein tensors connect transport and tidal effects to divergence-free geometry, while Bianchi identities and scalar invariants provide consistency and diagnostic tools.

title: Module overview
body: This module develops the matter side of general relativity. Stress-energy, perfect-fluid models, energy conditions, covariant conservation, and equations of state describe local sources and the assumptions needed to connect them consistently to spacetime geometry.

title: Module overview
body: This module brings geometry and matter together in Einstein's field equations. It introduces the cosmological term, variational derivation, matter-action source, trace-reversed form, and vacuum equations while keeping conventions and special cases explicit.

title: Module overview
body: This module connects Einstein gravity to weak-field observations and Newtonian intuition. Metric perturbations, the Newtonian limit, redshift, light bending, perihelion advance, and post-Newtonian bookkeeping show how measurable corrections emerge from the full theory.

title: Module overview
body: This module develops the central exact vacuum geometry around a spherical mass. The Schwarzschild metric and radius lead to horizons, the distinction between coordinate and curvature singularities, and an effective-potential description of timelike and null orbits.

title: Module overview
body: This module supplies the minimal geometric language needed when spacetime can no longer be covered by one global inertial coordinate system. Manifolds, charts, coordinate transformations, worldlines, tangent spaces, and cotangent spaces provide the local stage on which GR is written.

title: Module overview
body: This module collects the reusable tensor notation needed by GR and later physics topics. Tensor fields, index conventions, and transformation laws explain how equations can use coordinate components while still making coordinate-independent statements.

title: Module overview
body: This module states the core physical assumptions of special relativity: inertial frames, the constancy of light speed, and the principle of relativity. These postulates set the constraints that force a new geometry of space and time.

title: Module overview
body: This module introduces events as the basic spacetime objects and locality as the rule that physical laws are tested in small neighbourhoods. It prepares the move from everyday observer language to precise spacetime geometry.

title: Module overview
body: This module develops the flat spacetime geometry of SR. The metric, interval, Lorentz transformations, light cones, and Minkowski diagrams turn the postulates into a geometric framework where different inertial observers agree on invariant structure.

title: Module overview
body: This module builds the main particle-kinematics tools of SR. Proper time and four-vectors lead to position, velocity, momentum, and mass-energy equivalence as invariant ways to describe motion and energy.

title: Module overview
body: This module recasts mechanics in the action-based language used throughout modern field theory. Lagrangians, Euler-Lagrange equations, canonical momentum, Hamiltonian ideas, and Noether's theorem connect dynamics with symmetry and conservation.

title: Module overview
body: This module shifts attention from particles to fields. Scalar and vector fields, field Lagrangians, and field equations establish the local dynamical language needed for electromagnetism and later relativistic field theories.

title: Module overview
body: This module builds the relativistic electromagnetic field from potentials, the field tensor, electric and magnetic components, four-current, and Maxwell's equations. It shows how familiar electromagnetism fits into the spacetime language of SR.

title: Module overview
body: This module explains how charged matter interacts with the electromagnetic potential and why gauge freedom is not optional decoration. Gauge invariance, minimal coupling, the Lorentz force, charge conservation, and Lorenz gauge form the main interaction toolkit.

title: Module overview
body: This module tracks energy and momentum carried by fields. The energy-momentum tensor, electromagnetic stress-energy, energy density, and Poynting vector connect local field dynamics to conserved flow of energy and momentum.

title: Module overview
body: This module studies propagating disturbances in relativistic fields. The wave equation, electromagnetic waves, and radiation reaction show how field equations produce radiation and how emitted fields carry energy and momentum away.

title: Module overview
body: This module gathers higher-level symmetry ideas that organise the earlier material. Lorentz invariance and gauge fixing clarify which structures are physically meaningful and which are choices of description.
